## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis accesses the trained HSTU through a host ModelView; backbone internals are not supplied here. `item_emb.weight` provides item representations, `log2feats(sequence)` produces per-position sequence features, and `predict_score(features, items)` scores candidates. Paired probes extract the feature at the greatest nonzero sequence index, correctly handling left padding.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` retains `view.model`, metadata, review-data interfaces, and training histories. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with B × L tensors. Paired probes use `user_train['History']` and optional aligned timestamps. `run_full_diagnosis` temporarily enables evaluation mode, disables gradients, and restores model mode and Python, NumPy, and Torch RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding cosine:** Mean off-diagonal cosine among up to 2,048 sampled real-item embeddings, excluding invalid or near-zero rows. Higher values indicate stronger directional alignment; cosine alone cannot establish collapse or ranking failure.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Across at most ten loader batches, measure mean margin, tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer negative-winning positions generally indicate better sampled separation; the 0.5 threshold depends on score scale. Padding and nonfinite margins are excluded.
- **Paired ranking:** For at most 200 eligible training users, reserve the final training item as target and score it against 99 unique unseen negatives. Report HR@10, target rank, changes from intact history, and top-10 overlap, with paired bootstrap intervals.

# Perturbation & Tests

Compare intact histories with a last-ten suffix, equal-sized recent-context and old-context deletions, and final-item removal. These reveal ranking sensitivity to context location and the latest observed item. Retained histories are compacted and left-padded without backfill, so deletion changes evidence and positions jointly. Anchor removal also changes the readout item.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The result contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`; `paired_recent_context` includes user records, condition summaries, missingness, settings, and a JSON artifact path. The interpreter prompt requests status, findings, implications, and supporting evidence.

Ranking probes are in-sample, not host validation. Intervals condition on fitted weights and fixed candidates. Item-category breakdowns, geometry-preserving masks, and single-report four-category macro estimates are unavailable. Timestamps are recorded but not consumed by HSTU. No causal intent, simulator traits, or guaranteed generalization is established.

Compare removing recent preceding items with removing equally many randomly selected preceding items. Separately replace items in place using frequency-matched training items, preserving occupied positions, timestamps and masks; compare recent-position replacements with equal-size random-position replacements. Deletion changes content and sequence geometry, whereas replacement preserves geometry but introduces substitute content. Use explicit position/time-preserving attention-edge interventions only where supported; inserting padding can alter masking and positional indexing. These experiments establish intervention-specific computational sensitivity, not user intent or real-world causal preference. It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
family-specific sequential-model compatibility contract; preserve the host ModelView interfaces and adapt probes to that family. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis accesses the trained HSTU through a host ModelView; backbone internals are not supplied here. `item_emb.weight` provides item representations, `log2feats(sequence)` produces per-position sequence features, and `predict_score(features, items)` scores candidates. Paired probes extract the feature at the greatest nonzero sequence index, correctly handling left padding.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` retains `view.model`, metadata, review-data interfaces, and training histories. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with B × L tensors. Paired probes use `user_train['History']` and optional aligned timestamps. `run_full_diagnosis` temporarily enables evaluation mode, disables gradients, and restores model mode and Python, NumPy, and Torch RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding cosine:** Mean off-diagonal cosine among up to 2,048 sampled real-item embeddings, excluding invalid or near-zero rows. Higher values indicate stronger directional alignment; cosine alone cannot establish collapse or ranking failure.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Across at most ten loader batches, measure mean margin, tenth percentile, fraction below zero, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer negative-winning positions generally indicate better sampled separation; the 0.5 threshold depends on score scale. Padding and nonfinite margins are excluded.
- **Paired ranking:** For at most 200 eligible training users, reserve the final training item as target and score it against 99 unique unseen negatives. Report HR@10, target rank, changes from intact history, and top-10 overlap, with paired bootstrap intervals.

# Perturbation & Tests

Compare intact histories with a last-ten suffix, equal-sized recent-context and old-context deletions, and final-item removal. These reveal ranking sensitivity to context location and the latest observed item. Retained histories are compacted and left-padded without backfill, so deletion changes evidence and positions jointly. Anchor removal also changes the readout item.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The result contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`; `paired_recent_context` includes user records, condition summaries, missingness, settings, and a JSON artifact path. The interpreter prompt requests status, findings, implications, and supporting evidence.

Ranking probes are in-sample, not host validation. Intervals condition on fitted weights and fixed candidates. Item-category breakdowns, geometry-preserving masks, and single-report four-category macro estimates are unavailable. Timestamps are recorded but not consumed by HSTU. No causal intent, simulator traits, or guaranteed generalization is established.
